a53_tail: So under its best farther-reaching rule the half-particle background is the best state found on large grids, but not yet shown to be the calmest.
a56_bullet: - **The cube rival is closer than it looked (A56; its bookkeeping rechecked by me).** Exact 24-place calculations show that cubes joined face to face gain almost exactly what the earlier estimate assumed, but cubes that touch along an edge gain much more, a contact the estimate left out; crowding by neighbouring cubes then cancels most of that gain, and the bookkeeping does not settle at three cubes (exact block energies; the crystal estimate is argued). A 24-place block of edge-sharing cubes already sits within 0.008 per place of the background, despite its open edges. So whether the background or a crystal of linked cubes is the calmest state of this rule is genuinely open; settling it needs a better variational cube state or larger calculations than this machine allows.
s17_old: The far-lower states on small exactly solvable grids turned out to be quirks of how those grids wrap (A53). A near-tie with loosely linked cubes is unsettled.
s17_new: The far-lower states on small exactly solvable grids turned out to be quirks of how those grids wrap (A53). A crystal of linked cubes is a close rival and the contest is open: edge-sharing cubes come within 0.008 per place (A56).
